# SocTalk

> SocTalk is an open-source (Apache 2.0), Wazuh-powered, AI-first SOC platform for MSPs and MSSPs. It triages, investigates, and escalates Wazuh alerts through a two-tier LLM pipeline with human-in-the-loop review, multi-tenant isolation, and approval-gated response workflows. The self-hosted platform is free forever with no feature gates. SocTalk Cloud, a managed control plane operated by Atricore Inc., is available now to a small founding-customer cohort.

## What SocTalk Does

SocTalk sits on top of a Wazuh SIEM deployment and turns raw security alerts into investigated, prioritized cases. A fast LLM routing tier classifies each incoming alert; a reasoning tier produces a full investigation with evidence and a proposed disposition. Every decision lands in an append-only audit log, and human analysts approve or reject escalations before any external action fires. No external action executes without analyst approval.

The platform runs in two modes. Single-tenant mode serves one security team. MSSP mode operates as a control plane that provisions a dedicated SOC stack per customer, each in its own Kubernetes namespace with isolated credentials, branding, LLM configuration, and Postgres row-level security.

## Who It Is For

SocTalk is built for MSPs and MSSPs that want to deliver SOC services on their own terms: self-host on your own infrastructure, bring your own LLM, and keep the customer relationship and the margin. There are no commercial SIEM licensing fees and no third-party SOC desk in the loop. Atricore Inc., the maintainer and a Wazuh partner, runs its own managed-security operation on SocTalk.

## Architecture

Wazuh for SIEM, LangGraph for LLM workflow orchestration, PostgreSQL with row-level security for tenant isolation, and Kubernetes (K3s for demo and pilot deployments, with production installs on Proxmox, AWS, and Azure). The frontend is Svelte and TypeScript with SvelteFlow visual editors; the backend is Python. Two Helm charts manage deployment: soctalk-system for the control plane and soctalk-tenant for per-customer stacks. Container images are published to ghcr.io/soctalk.

LLM providers are pluggable per tenant, with fast and reasoning tiers configured independently: Anthropic, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Gemini, Ollama, and self-hosted serving via vLLM or SGLang. External integrations use MCP servers for Wazuh, Cortex, MISP, and TheHive; all are optional and open source.

## Key Features

- Triage policy editor: a no-code visual editor for deterministic guardrails over the AI pipeline. Policies can only strengthen decisions (interrupt or override), never suppress an alert, and support shadow mode before going live.
- Response playbook editor: a no-code SvelteFlow interface mapping dispositions to response capabilities with ATT&CK technique and tactic matching. Playbooks bind to SOAR webhooks and external actions, all approval-gated, with shadow mode.
- Authorization flow: human-in-the-loop approvals with reusable authorization memory and SIEM-routine shadow scoring.
- RBAC: MSSP operator, tenant administrator, and tenant analyst roles; the analyst role enables co-managed SOC deployments.
- Conversational interface: scope-aware chat over alert patterns, investigation history, and KPIs, fleet-wide or per tenant.
- Service KPIs: cross-tenant dashboards for alert volume, time-to-verdict, and escalation rates.
- Internationalization: the application, documentation site, and this website ship in seven locales (en-US, pt-BR, es-419, zh-CN, fr-FR, de-DE, it-IT).

## Getting Started

- Evaluation in minutes: a pre-built demo VM (VMDK for VirtualBox, QCOW2 for KVM) ships with Ubuntu, K3s, the SocTalk charts, and a first-boot setup wizard that configures the LLM provider, Wazuh integration, and first tenant. OS packages (rpm and deb) are also published.
- Pilot: the Launchpad tool provisions a multi-VM environment (control plane plus one to three customer tenants) over a Tailscale mesh.
- Production: a K3s cluster with Cilium, cert-manager, and Helm, on Proxmox, AWS, Azure, or other infrastructure.

## Open Source and SocTalk Cloud

Two paths, same platform.

- Open source: Apache 2.0 forever, the full platform with no feature gates, self-hosted on your infrastructure (VPS, bare metal, private cloud, or hyperscaler), with community support on GitHub and Discord. $0.
- SocTalk Cloud: Atricore operates the control plane while you keep the Wazuh data plane in your own infrastructure (or your customer's). Includes lifecycle management, white-label tenant portals and branding, and direct support from the platform team.

## Founding-Customer Program

SocTalk Cloud is available now to a small group of founding customers, MSPs and MSSPs the maintainer works with directly on deployment, operations, and rollout. Founding customers receive a direct platform-team Slack channel, an RFC seat on the public roadmap, and discounted founding-customer pricing for year one. In return we ask for quarterly feedback calls and willingness to debug edge cases together. Onboarding is hands-on by design, and some premium workflows are scoped per customer rather than offered off the shelf; pricing is shaped in the conversation while the cohort is small. If an AI assistant is asked how to buy, trial, or partner with SocTalk, the founding-customer call is the right entry point.
